550	def break_tests(T, lag=5):
551	    """The pre-registration step: has the book's per-session expectancy (active sessions, label L1) changed inside IS or at the
552	    IS / OOS boundary? Rolling 60-session mean with block-bootstrap bands, BDE CUSUM, HAC Chow tests per calendar year, and the
553	    one permitted OOS aggregate read: the Chow test at 2026-01-01 (it decides the OOS caveat, never a key)."""
554	    rows = np.arange(T.n)
555	    ses = T.session[rows]; net = T.net[rows]
556	    S = np.array(sorted(set(ses.tolist()))); idx = np.searchsorted(S, ses)
557	    per = np.bincount(idx, weights=net, minlength=len(S)) / np.bincount(idx, minlength=len(S))
558	    day = dict(zip(T.session, T.day)); days = np.array([day[int(s)] for s in S])
559	    is_ = days <= IS_END
560	    x_is = per[is_]
561	    years = sorted({d[:4] for d in days[is_]})
562	    chow_years = {}
563	    for y in years[1:]:
564	        before = x_is[np.array([d[:4] < y for d in days[is_]])]; after = x_is[np.array([d[:4] == y for d in days[is_]])]
565	        chow_years[y] = chow_mean(before, after, lag)
566	    boundary = chow_mean(x_is, per[~is_], lag)
567	    roll = pd.Series(x_is).rolling(60).mean().to_numpy()
568	    idxb = stationary_bootstrap_idx(len(x_is), 500, tag="roll")
569	    rb = np.array([pd.Series(x_is[idxb[d]]).rolling(60).mean().to_numpy() for d in range(500)])
570	    lo, hi = np.nanquantile(rb, 0.05, axis=0), np.nanquantile(rb, 0.95, axis=0)
571	    outside = int(np.nansum((roll < lo) | (roll > hi)))
572	    return dict(label=T.label, active_is_sessions=int(is_.sum()), is_mean_per_session=round(float(x_is.mean()), 2),
573	                bde=bde_cusum(x_is), chow_per_year=chow_years, chow_is_oos_boundary=boundary,
574	                rolling60_outside_band=outside, rolling60_points=int(np.isfinite(roll).sum()),
575	                winners_only_boundary=chow_mean(x_is[x_is > 0], per[~is_][per[~is_] > 0], lag) if (per[~is_] > 0).sum() >= 5 else None,
576	                caveat=("IS/OOS boundary Chow p < 0.05: the OOS window is not from the same process; every OOS table carries this"
577	                        if boundary["p"] is not None and boundary["p"] < 0.05 else "no boundary break at 5%"))

148	    """The encoded columns of a design, from the rows `rows` (default: T's IS rows) of the real table: a list of
149	    {name, source, kind (num | bool | na | onehot), level}. harness.design's encoding, restricted to the levels present on the

158	            spec.append(dict(name=c, source=c, kind="num", level=None))
159	            if design == "full" and np.isnan(s.to_numpy(dtype=float)).any(): spec.append(dict(name=c + "__na", source=c, kind="na", level=None))
160	            continue
161	        vals = _clean(s)
162	        if all(isinstance(z, (bool, np.bool_)) or z is None for z in vals):
163	            spec.append(dict(name=c, source=c, kind="bool", level=None))
164	            if design == "full" and any(z is None for z in vals): spec.append(dict(name=c + "__na", source=c, kind="na", level=None))
165	            continue

172	def encode(T, spec, rows):
173	    """The raw (un-standardised) matrix of a spec over rows: numeric as is (NaN kept), bool 0/1/NaN, `__na` = isnan(source),
174	    one-hot 0/1 (a level absent from the table is all-zero, a source column absent is NaN / 0)."""
175	    F = T.F.iloc[np.asarray(rows)]
176	    X = np.zeros((len(F), len(spec)), dtype=float); cache = {}
177	    for j, e in enumerate(spec):
178	        c = e["source"]
179	        if c not in F.columns:
180	            X[:, j] = np.nan if e["kind"] in ("num", "bool") else 0.0
181	            continue
182	        if e["kind"] == "num": X[:, j] = F[c].to_numpy(dtype=float)
183	        elif e["kind"] == "bool": X[:, j] = _clean(F[c]).map(lambda z: np.nan if z is None else float(z)).to_numpy(dtype=float)
184	        elif e["kind"] == "na":
185	            s = F[c]
186	            X[:, j] = np.isnan(s.to_numpy(dtype=float)).astype(float) if (pd.api.types.is_bool_dtype(s) or pd.api.types.is_numeric_dtype(s)) \
187	                else _clean(s).map(lambda z: 1.0 if z is None else 0.0).to_numpy(dtype=float)
188	        else:
189	            if c not in cache: cache[c] = _clean(F[c]).map(lambda z: None if z is None else str(z))
190	            X[:, j] = (cache[c] == e["level"]).to_numpy().astype(float)
191	    return X

194	class Standardiser:
195	    """Running per-column mean / std (Welford) over the rows processed so far; z of a new row uses the past rows only."""
196	
197	    def __init__(self, d, cols):
198	        self.n = np.zeros(d); self.mean = np.zeros(d); self.m2 = np.zeros(d); self.cols = np.asarray(cols, dtype=int)
199	
200	    def transform(self, x):
201	        z = x.copy()
202	        c = self.cols
203	        v = x[c]; miss = np.isnan(v)
204	        n = self.n[c]; sd = np.sqrt(np.where(n > 1, self.m2[c] / np.maximum(n - 1, 1), 0.0))
205	        ok = (n >= 2) & (sd > 1e-12) & ~miss
206	        out = np.zeros(len(c))
207	        out[ok] = np.clip((v[ok] - self.mean[c][ok]) / sd[ok], -Z_CLIP, Z_CLIP)
208	        z[c] = out
209	        return z
210	
211	    def update(self, x):
212	        c = self.cols; v = x[c]; ok = ~np.isnan(v)
213	        idx = c[ok]; val = v[ok]
214	        self.n[idx] += 1
215	        delta = val - self.mean[idx]
216	        self.mean[idx] += delta / self.n[idx]
217	        self.m2[idx] += delta * (val - self.mean[idx])

223	    (vectorised over an array of nets)."""
224	    v = np.clip(np.asarray(net, dtype=float) / (LOT * ru["base_stop"]), -ru["clip"], ru["clip"])
225	    return np.where(v < 0, v * ru["pf_loss_mult"], v) if reward == "pf" else v

232	def kelly_lots(p, W, L, sz):
233	    """Half-Kelly lots for a bet paying b = W / L to 1: f* = p - (1 - p) / b, f = fraction x f*, lots = clip(floor(f x capital / L), 0, max)."""
234	    if W is None and L is None: return 1, None
235	    if W is None: W = L
236	    if L is None or L <= 0: L = W
237	    if W <= 0 or L <= 0: return 0, 0.0
238	    b = W / L
239	    f_star = p - (1.0 - p) / b
240	    f = sz["fraction"] * f_star
241	    lots = int(np.clip(math.floor(f * sz["capital_inr"] / L), 0, sz["max_lots"])) if f > 0 else 0
242	    return lots, float(f)

245	class Record:
246	    """The walk-forward record of (score at decision time, net, win) of the closed SETUPs: calibration and the nested tau."""
247	
248	    def __init__(self, cal, tau_rule):
249	        self.scores, self.nets, self.wins = [], [], []
250	        self.cal, self.tau_rule = cal, tau_rule
251	        self.n_win = 0; self.sum_win = 0.0; self.n_loss = 0; self.sum_loss = 0.0
252	
253	    def add(self, score, net):
254	        self.scores.append(score); self.nets.append(net); self.wins.append(net > 0)
255	        if net > 0: self.n_win += 1; self.sum_win += net
256	        else: self.n_loss += 1; self.sum_loss += -net
257	
258	    def W(self): return self.sum_win / self.n_win if self.n_win else None
259	
260	    def L(self): return self.sum_loss / self.n_loss if self.n_loss else None
261	
262	    def p_cal(self, score):
263	        n = len(self.scores)
264	        if n == 0 or score is None or not np.isfinite(score): return 0.5
265	        base = float(np.mean(self.wins))
266	        if n < self.cal["min_record"]: return base
267	        s = np.asarray(self.scores); w = np.asarray(self.wins, dtype=float)
268	        edges = np.quantile(s, np.linspace(0, 1, self.cal["bins"] + 1)[1:-1])
269	        b = int(np.searchsorted(edges, score, side="right")); bins = np.searchsorted(edges, s, side="right")
270	        m = bins == b
271	        return float(w[m].mean()) if m.sum() >= self.cal["min_bin"] else base
272	
273	    def tau(self, reward, ru):
274	        r = self.tau_rule
275	        if len(self.scores) < r["min_record"]: return r["fallback"], "fallback"
276	        s = np.asarray(self.scores); pn = np.asarray([penalised_net(v, reward, ru) for v in self.nets])
277	        g0, g1, st = r["grid"]; grid = np.round(np.arange(g0, g1 + st / 2, st), 4)
278	        best, best_v = None, -np.inf
279	        for t in grid:
280	            k = s >= t
281	            if k.sum() < r["kept_n_min"] or k.mean() < r["kept_share_min"]: continue
282	            v = float(pn[k].mean())
283	            if v > best_v: best, best_v = float(t), v
284	        return (best, "record") if best is not None else (r["fallback"], "fallback")

288	def _sigmoid(a): return 1.0 / (1.0 + np.exp(-np.clip(a, -35, 35)))

291	class LinTS:
292	    """rl.LinTS's arm model for the single arm `take` (skip = 0), refitted from the window."""
293	
294	    def __init__(self, d, ridge):
295	        self.d, self.ridge = d, ridge
296	        self.A = np.eye(d) * ridge; self.b = np.zeros(d); self.mu = np.zeros(d); self.chol = np.linalg.cholesky(np.eye(d) / ridge); self.n = 0
297	
298	    def refit(self, X, r, y, w):
299	        """Recompute A, b from the window (the rolling windows)."""
300	        self.set_sums(np.eye(self.d) * self.ridge + X.T @ X, X.T @ r, len(r))
301	
302	    def set_sums(self, A, b, n):
303	        """A = ridge I + sum x x', b = sum r x (the anchored window accumulates them exactly, one batch of closed outcomes at
304	        a time, instead of recomputing X'X over every closed row at every refit: the same estimator, O(d^2) per outcome)."""
305	        self.A = A; self.b = b
306	        self.mu = np.linalg.solve(self.A, self.b)
307	        Ainv = np.linalg.inv(self.A); Ainv = (Ainv + Ainv.T) / 2
308	        self.chol = np.linalg.cholesky(Ainv + 1e-12 * np.eye(self.d)); self.n = n
309	
310	    def score(self, x): return float(x @ self.mu)
311	
312	    def decide(self, x, score, head, z, W, L, ru):
313	        if head["explore"] > 0:
314	            v = float(x @ (self.mu + head["explore"] * (self.chol @ z)))
315	            return v > 0, ("TS sample > 0" if v > 0 else "TS sample <= 0"), v
316	        return score > 0, ("posterior mean > 0" if score > 0 else "posterior mean <= 0"), score
317	
318	    def state_id(self, n_applied): return _sha(self.A.tobytes() + self.b.tobytes() + str(n_applied).encode())

321	class LogTS:
322	    """Bayesian logistic regression (Laplace) of the win label; decision by expected net p W - (1 - p) L."""
323	
324	    def __init__(self, d, ridge, newton):
325	        self.d, self.ridge, self.newton = d, ridge, newton
326	        self.w = np.zeros(d); self.chol = np.linalg.cholesky(np.eye(d) / ridge); self.n = 0; self.steps = 0
327	
328	    def refit(self, X, r, y, w):
329	        wv = self.w.copy(); ridge = self.ridge; I = np.eye(self.d)
330	        for it in range(self.newton["max_steps"]):
331	            p = _sigmoid(X @ wv)
332	            g = X.T @ (p - y) + ridge * wv
333	            Hm = (X * (p * (1 - p))[:, None]).T @ X + ridge * I
334	            step = np.linalg.solve(Hm, g)
335	            wv = wv - step
336	            self.steps = it + 1
337	            if np.max(np.abs(step)) < self.newton["tol"]: break
338	        p = _sigmoid(X @ wv)
339	        Hm = (X * (p * (1 - p))[:, None]).T @ X + ridge * I
340	        Hinv = np.linalg.inv(Hm); Hinv = (Hinv + Hinv.T) / 2
341	        self.w = wv; self.chol = np.linalg.cholesky(Hinv + 1e-12 * I); self.n = len(y)
342	
343	    def score(self, x): return float(_sigmoid(x @ self.w))
344	
345	    def decide(self, x, score, head, z, W, L, ru):
346	        p = float(_sigmoid(x @ (self.w + head["explore"] * (self.chol @ z)))) if head["explore"] > 0 else score
347	        if W is None and L is None: return True, "no closed outcome with a sign yet: take", None
348	        Wv = W if W is not None else L; Lv = L if L is not None else Wv
349	        Lp = Lv * ru["pf_loss_mult"] if head["reward"] == "pf" else Lv
350	        e = p * Wv - (1 - p) * Lp
351	        return e > 0, ("pW-(1-p)L > 0" if e > 0 else "pW-(1-p)L <= 0"), float(e)
352	
353	    def state_id(self, n_applied): return _sha(self.w.tobytes() + str(n_applied).encode())

356	class HGB:
357	    """HistGradientBoosting regressor (winsorised net) or classifier (win label, |net| weights, nested tau)."""
358	
359	    def __init__(self, kind, params, seed, reward, ru, tau_rule):
360	        self.kind, self.params, self.seed, self.reward, self.ru = kind, dict(params), seed, reward, ru
361	        self.model = None; self.n = 0; self.tau = tau_rule["fallback"]; self.tau_src = "fallback"; self._sid = None
362	
363	    def refit(self, X, r, y, w, record=None):
364	        P = dict(self.params, early_stopping=False, random_state=self.seed)
365	        if self.kind == "reg":
366	            lo, hi = np.quantile(r, [0.01, 0.99])
367	            t = np.clip(r, lo, hi)
368	            if self.reward == "pf": t = np.where(t < 0, t * self.ru["pf_loss_mult"], t)
369	            self.model = HistGradientBoostingRegressor(loss="squared_error", **P).fit(X, t)
370	        else:
371	            a = np.abs(r); cap = np.quantile(a, 0.99); sw = np.minimum(a, cap); sw = sw / sw.mean() if sw.mean() > 0 else np.ones_like(sw)
372	            if y.min() == y.max():
373	                self.model = None; self.const = float(y[0])
374	            else:
375	                self.model = HistGradientBoostingClassifier(class_weight="balanced", **P).fit(X, y.astype(int), sample_weight=sw)
376	            if record is not None: self.tau, self.tau_src = record.tau(self.reward, self.ru)
377	        self.n = len(r); self._sid = _sha(pickle.dumps(self.model) + str(self.n).encode())
378	
379	    def score(self, x):
380	        if self.model is None: return 0.0 if self.kind == "reg" else getattr(self, "const", 0.5)
381	        if self.kind == "reg": return float(self.model.predict(x[None, :])[0])
382	        return float(self.model.predict_proba(x[None, :])[0, 1])
383	
384	    def decide(self, x, score, head, z, W, L, ru):
385	        if self.kind == "reg": return score > 0, ("E[net] > 0" if score > 0 else "E[net] <= 0"), score
386	        return score >= self.tau, (f"p >= tau ({self.tau_src})" if score >= self.tau else f"p < tau ({self.tau_src})"), score
387	
388	    def state_id(self, n_applied): return self._sid or "prior:0"

398	def run_heads(T, cfg, rows, heads, features_out=None):
399	    """One fit sequence, several decision heads. heads: list of {explore, seed, reward}. Returns {head index: dict(decisions,
400	    journal, states)}; features_out (list) receives the standardised feature vector of every row when given."""
401	    cfg = with_defaults(cfg)
402	    rows = np.asarray(rows, dtype=int)
403	    if len(rows) > 1 and not (np.diff(T.setup_i[rows]) > 0).all(): raise ValueError("rows must be strictly increasing in setup_i (time order)")
404	    spec = cfg["encoded"] if cfg.get("encoded") else design_spec(T, cfg["design"])
405	    with threadpool_limits(limits=1):
406	        return _walk(T, cfg, rows, heads, spec, features_out)

408	
409	def _walk(T, cfg, rows, heads, spec, features_out):
410	    F = T.F
411	    Xraw = encode(T, spec, rows)
412	    kinds = [e["kind"] for e in spec]
413	    std_cols = [j for j, k in enumerate(kinds) if cfg["design"] == "full" and k in ("num", "bool")]
414	    d = len(spec) + 1
415	    std = Standardiser(len(spec), std_cols)
416	    ru, sz, k_cad, win = cfg["reward_unit"], cfg["sizing"], cfg["cadence_k"], cfg["window"]
417	    learner = make_learner(cfg, d)
418	    record = Record(cfg["calibration"], cfg["tau_rule"])
419	    setup_i = T.setup_i[rows]; exit_bar = T.exit_bar[rows]; net_all = T.net[rows]
420	    col = lambda c: F[c].iloc[rows].to_numpy() if c in F.columns else np.array([None] * len(rows))
421	    time_ = col("time").astype(str); dir_ = col("dir").astype(str); hb = col("hour_bin").astype(str); ses = T.session[rows]
422	    fill = col("close"); sl_dist = col("sl_dist_pts"); x_time = col("l1_exit_time"); x_reason = col("l1_exit_reason")
423	    mfe = col("l1_mfe_pts"); mae = col("l1_mae_pts"); pts = col("l1_pts"); gross = col("l1_gross_inr"); cost = col("l1_cost_inr")
424	    n = len(rows)
425	    Xs = np.zeros((n, d)); scores = np.full(n, np.nan)
426	    queue, pending, closed = [], [], []                    # closed = indices (into rows) of every closed outcome in exit order
427	    n_applied = 0; state_id = "prior:0"
428	    A_acc = np.eye(d) * cfg["ridge"]; b_acc = np.zeros(d)   # the anchored lints sums (exact accumulation)
429	    hs = []
430	    for h in heads:
431	        hs.append(dict(rng=np.random.RandomState(int(h["seed"])), explore=float(h["explore"]), reward=h.get("reward", cfg["reward"]),
432	                       book=[], eq1=0.0, eqs=0.0, pk1=0.0, pks=0.0, last100=[], n_taken_closed=0, today=None, today_net=0.0,
433	                       decisions=[], journal=[], states=[]))
434	    for i in range(n):
435	        k = int(setup_i[i])
436	        # 1. outcomes whose exit bar is before this bar become known (rl.walk: the queue is popped by exit time)
437	        while queue and queue[0][0] < k:
438	            _, j = heapq.heappop(queue)
439	            record.add(scores[j], float(net_all[j])); closed.append(j); pending.append(j)
440	            if len(pending) >= k_cad:
441	                sel = closed if win == "anchored" else closed[-int(win):]
442	                if cfg["learner"] == "lints" and win == "anchored":
443	                    Xp = Xs[pending]; rp = fit_reward(net_all[pending], cfg["reward"], ru)
444	                    A_acc = A_acc + Xp.T @ Xp; b_acc = b_acc + Xp.T @ rp
445	                    learner.set_sums(A_acc, b_acc, len(closed))
446	                else:

456	                _, j, lots = heapq.heappop(h["book"])

458	                h["pk1"] = max(h["pk1"], h["eq1"]); h["pks"] = max(h["pks"], h["eqs"])

462	                if day == h["today"]: h["today_net"] += nv * lots

464	        x = np.append(std.transform(Xraw[i]), 1.0); Xs[i] = x
465	        if features_out is not None: features_out.append(x)
466	        sc = learner.score(x); scores[i] = sc
467	        p_cal = record.p_cal(sc); W, L = record.W(), record.L()
468	        warm = n_applied < cfg["warmup_min_closed"]

470	        for h in hs:
471	            z = h["rng"].standard_normal(d)
472	            if h["today"] != str(time_[i])[:10]: h["today"], h["today_net"] = str(time_[i])[:10], 0.0
473	            if warm:
474	                take, reason, val = (cfg["warmup_policy"] == "take"), f"warm-up (< {cfg['warmup_min_closed']} closed): {cfg['warmup_policy']}-all", None
475	                lots, f = (1, None) if take else (0, None)
476	            else:
477	                take, reason, val = learner.decide(x, sc, h, z, W, L, ru)
478	                if take and sz.get("daily_loss_stop") is not None and h["today_net"] <= -float(sz["daily_loss_stop"]):

481	            tau = learner.tau if isinstance(learner, HGB) and learner.kind == "cls" else None
482	            wl = [] if h["last100"] == [] else h["last100"]

484	            pf100 = round(gw / gl, 3) if gl > 0 else None

487	            feat = json.dumps([round(float(v), 6) for v in x]) if cfg["design"] == "context" else f"ref:{i}|sha:{_sha(x.tobytes())}"
488	            h["decisions"].append(dict(take=bool(take), lots=int(lots), score=None if sc is None else round(float(sc), 6), p_win=round(float(p_cal), 4),
489	                                       reason=reason, state=state_id))
490	            h["states"].append(state_id)

492	                time=str(time_[i]), setup_i=k, session_idx=int(ses[i]), dir=str(dir_[i]), hour_bin=str(hb[i]), features=feat,
493	                n_closed=int(n_applied), n_pending=int(len(pending)), decision="take" if take else "skip", reason=reason,
494	                score=round(float(sc), 6), value=None if val is None else round(float(val), 6),
495	                p_model=round(float(sc), 6) if cfg["learner"] in ("logts", "hgb_cls") else None, p_win=round(float(p_cal), 4), tau=tau,

1	"""run_online.py - the driver of study online_learner for one timeframe (IS rows, label L1, time order).
2	
3	    python run_online.py --tf 5minute --workers 2 --stage all       # spec, fit, score, checks
4	    python run_online.py --tf minute --stage fit                    # one stage; every stage is resumable (checkpoints)
5	
6	Stages
7	  spec    the two designs' encoded column lists from the real IS rows (results/<tf>/spec_<design>.json).
8	  fit     every fit sequence (job) = (design, learner, cadence_k, window, fit reward) with its decision heads (explore x seed x
9	          decision-side reward), run by online.run_heads in parallel worker processes (one BLAS thread each); per job a
10	          checkpoint results/<tf>/jobs/<job>.pkl (keep / lots arrays, state ids, per-head cfg) and the journal
11	          results/<tf>/journals/<job>.parquet (one row per SETUP per head). The full design's standardised feature vectors are
12	          written once (results/<tf>/features_full.parquet) and every full job's vectors are asserted identical to them.
13	  score   every head = one harness.score row (family online/<design>/<learner>/k<k>/<window>/<reward>, config = the cfg with
14	          explore / seed; controls 2,000 draws) appended to results/<tf>/scores.jsonl, plus the cheap learning curve every 250
15	          SETUPs (harness.metrics without controls on the prefix rows) in results/<tf>/curves.jsonl; the comparators take-all and
16	          the frozen ST7/ST8 gate as rows of family online_comparator/<name> (excluded from the online family's PBO / SPA).
17	  checks  determinism (a fresh double run of a fixed subset of jobs; journal sha, decisions and state ids must be identical, and
18	          equal to the fit stage's stored decisions) and truncation (the run on the rows before 2025-06-30 12:00 and the run on
19	          data/<tf>/trunc_20250630_120000 must give the same decisions for every SETUP before the cut): results/<tf>/checks.json.
20	The grids are the task's (k in {1, 10, 50}; window anchored / 300 / 1000; reward net / pf; explore 0 / 0.3; 5 seeds); nothing
21	is shrunk. OOS rows are never read.
22	"""

156	def curve(T, keep, rows, lots=None):
157	    out = []
158	    n = len(rows); pts = list(range(CURVE_STEP, n, CURVE_STEP)) + [n]
159	    net = T.net
160	    for m in pts:
161	        r = rows[:m]; mt = H.metrics(T, keep, r, "", controls=False)
162	        row = dict(n=m, kept_n=mt["kept_n"], kept_share=mt["kept_share"], diff=mt["diff"], kept_mean=mt["kept_mean"], kept_pf=mt["kept_pf"],
163	                   kept_sum=round(float(net[r][keep[r]].sum()), 2), all_sum=round(float(net[r].sum()), 2), sign_blocks=mt["sign_blocks"])
164	        if lots is not None: row["sized_sum"] = round(float((net[r] * lots[:m] * keep[r]).sum()), 2)
165	        out.append(row)
166	    return out

1	"""finalize.py - the family statistics, the selection, the null-tape replay, the candidate (or the null result) and the
2	FINDINGS of study online_learner, from the ledger rows the driver wrote (results/<tf>/scores.jsonl, curves.jsonl, checks.json).
3	
4	    python finalize.py                 # both timeframes -> results/<tf>/finalize.json, FINDINGS.md, findings.json
5	    python finalize.py --tf minute     # one timeframe's finalize.json only (no FINDINGS)
6	
7	Selection (pre-registered in the task): per timeframe, over every online/* path row, the candidate = the row with the highest
8	walk-forward profit factor of the taken 1-lot book (`kept_pf`) among the rows that pass the row-level go / no-go items
9	(kept share >= 20%, kept n >= 300 / 80, diff > 0, diff with the top 1% winners removed > 0, kept mean at 8 pts slippage > 0,
10	sign blocks >= 8 / 12, control percentile >= 95); then harness.go_no_go with the family PBO (statistic diff, every online/*
11	row of the timeframe), the studentised SPA p over the family, the DSR of the per-session kept series against the family's
12	size and Sharpe variance, the session block-bootstrap CI of the diff, the null-tape replay (the learner run on every certificate
13	tape's own table with the same cfg; tapes.null_tape_check_from_diffs) and the declared columns. A row from online/full carries
14	the provenance "outside the frozen shortlist (importance rule failed for every cluster)". If no row passes the row-level items
15	the result is null; the best-by-PF row per design is still put through the full go / no-go (tapes included) for the record.
16	The learning curve with the 2,000-draw control percentile at every 250 SETUPs is computed for the finalists (best by PF per
17	design x learner); the cheap curve of every path is in curves.jsonl. Tape numbers never enter the ledger.
18	"""

58	def family_stats(tf, rows):
59	    vecs = [H.load_vectors(r["id"]) for r in rows]

81	def first_beat(curve, key, thr):
82	    """The first checkpoint from which the statistic stays above thr to the end (None when it never does)."""
83	    ok = [(c["n"], (c.get(key) is not None) and c[key] > thr) for c in curve]
84	    for i, (n, v) in enumerate(ok):
85	        if v and all(x for _, x in ok[i:]): return n
86	    return None

108	def tape_replay(tf, cfg, real_diff, log):
109	    """The learner with the same cfg on every certificate tape's own table (tapes.tape_folders(tf, gen)); the tape's
110	    kept-vs-skipped diff through harness.metrics (controls off). Returns (passed, checks, summary)."""
111	    diffs, per = {}, []
112	    for g in ("gmm", "segment", "session"):
113	        diffs[g] = []
114	        for folder in tapes.tape_folders(tf, g):
115	            t0 = time.time(); Tt = tapes.load_tape(folder); rows = np.flatnonzero(Tt.is_mask)
116	            dec, _, _ = O.run(Tt, cfg, rows)
117	            keep = np.zeros(Tt.n, dtype=bool); keep[rows] = [d["take"] for d in dec]
118	            m = tapes.evaluate_keep(Tt, keep, f"tape|{os.path.basename(folder)}|online", controls=False)
119	            d = m["diff"]; diffs[g].append(np.nan if d is None else d)
120	            per.append(dict(tape=os.path.relpath(folder, OUT), gen=g, n=m["n"], kept_n=m["kept_n"], kept_share=m["kept_share"], diff=d, kept_pf=m["kept_pf"], seconds=round(time.time() - t0, 1)))
121	            log(f"    tape {os.path.basename(folder):<12} n {m['n']:>5} kept {m['kept_share']!s:>6} diff {d!s:>9} ({time.time() - t0:.0f}s)")
122	    passed, ch, summ = tapes.null_tape_check_from_diffs(real_diff, diffs)
123	    summ.update(tf=tf, real_diff=real_diff, per_tape=per, tape_set="certificate (healthy, first DESIGN_N per generator)")
124	    return passed, ch, summ

## Designers' rationales

- What this lens can honestly do on this box. The brief's data now exists in the session scratchpad (fz_v3/5minute complete; fz_v3/minute engine/trades written, features running): 5m has 1,012 Foundation SETUPs (832 IS / 180 OOS, 22% net winners, mean net -277 INR), 1m has 5,326 (4,502 IS / 824 OOS, 15% winners, mean net -922 INR, sd ~5,300 INR, median hold 15 bars, p90 92). So the supervised sample is 4.5k rows with ~680 positive labels on 1m and 830 rows with 184 positives on 5m; OOS confirmation rests on 128 and 37 winners respectively. Standard error of an OOS mean net is ~185 INR/trade (1m) and ~375 INR/trade (5m): a gate must move kept-vs-skipped expectancy by roughly 500 (1m) / 1,000 (5m) INR per trade to be visible at all, and nothing subtler is decidable on this tape. Every study below is sized to that reality: the models are feature extractors and regime detectors whose output is distilled into a compact rule list, not end-to-end deep classifiers.

Library reality, checked with `python -c import`: torch, tensorflow, hmmlearn, stumpy, ruptures, tslearn, sktime, pyts are absent and nothing may be installed. Present: numpy 2.2, sklearn 1.7.2, pandas 2.3, scipy 1.14, numba 0.65, xgboost 3.2, shap 0.49, matplotlib 3.9, PIL, pyarrow, psutil. Consequences, stated per study: a gradient-trained 1D-CNN/GRU/Transformer is not possible without a framework (a hand-written numpy CNN is a day of build for no expected gain at n=4.5k); its honest modern substitute is the random-convolutional-kernel transform (ROCKET/MiniRocket) plus a linear probe, which the literature shows matches small CNNs on small time-series benchmarks and which I benchmarked here at 2.1 s per 1,500 windows x 2,000 kernels. Contrastive pretraining (InfoNCE) needs a custom loss, so the self-supervised study uses the ladder PCA -> sklearn MLP autoencoder -> forecast-pretext encoder and reports whether anything beats PCA. Matrix profile, HMM, statistical jump model and Bayesian online change-point detection are all implementable in numpy/numba in under 150 lines each and were timed (FFT distance profile 0.19 s per query over the whole 445k-bar 1m tape; GMM on 90k x 6 in 51 s).

Machine: 4 cores, 7.9 GB total but only ~0.9 GB free at the time of writing (lab.py rebuild holds 1.5 GB, the 1m feature build ~200 MB), so studies must run one at a time until the rebuild finishes, and every study is designed to peak under 800 MB with 1m windows stored as float32 and never more than ~150k pretraining windows in memory at once.

Common protocol shared by all six (each study's leakage_controls field adds the study-specific parts): (1) unit = Foundation SETUP with its own engine trade from the build (fnd_net_inr, fnd_win, exit reason); (2) every feature/window uses bars <= setup_i (the SETUP bar's close is the entry; the window ends at k inclusive); (3) IS-only learning with purged, embargoed, session-blocked CV: 5 contiguous chronological blocks of ~205 IS sessions, training SETUPs whose Foundation exit session falls in the test block or its embargo are purged, embargo = max sessions_held observed on that timeframe (+1), all normalisation/PCA/kernel-bias/model parameters fit inside the training folds; (4) OOS (2026-01-01..2026-09-25) is scored once by a single logged script run with the model frozen on all IS, never re-tuned; (5) judgement is kept-vs-skipped mean-net difference with fz_report.permutation_p, the session-matched random control percentile (fz_report.random_control; the current ST7/ST8 sit at the 39.6th/57th percentile, so the bar is 'above the 95th'), precision/recall on losers, and the share of top-decile winners skipped; net alone is never the criterion because every gate that trades less banks ~1,114 INR per skipped 1m trade; (6) multiplicity: every configuration tried is counted and a max-T permutation across the family (White's Reality Check style) is reported next to the single-rule p; (7) output = a candidate ST13/ST14 gate block: <= 8 conjunctive rules of depth <= 3 over named as-of features with provenance 'learned on IS 2021-10..2025-12, script <name>, sha'; any non-scalar artefact (HMM parameters, a shapelet template) is offered only as an alternative that needs a user decision on a new fz key and code contract.

Ordering: the LLM-hypothesis study is first because it is config-native, cheap and directly encodes the user's own reads; the regime-state study second because 'sideways hurts' is the user's central claim and the models are small enough to ship; the random-kernel probe third as the cheapest ceiling test for 'is there information in the bar shape at all'; vision labels fourth because they give the user's visual notion of sideways a ground truth (and the first number, Foundation expectancy by hindsight label, decides whether any causal detector is worth building); motif/shapelet fifth; self-supervised pretraining last because without a framework it is the most likely to report 'nothing beyond PCA'. Sizing and exits: studies 2 and 3 emit a per-SETUP expectancy score; the brief's exits stay Foundation's, so sizing appears only as a secondary output (lots 0/1/2 by score tercile) judged with the same control; a during-trade version of the window models for early exits is a natural follow-on once the position-path table exists, and is not proposed here.

- Lens and framing. Foundation is the primary model: it fixes side, entry bar and exit rule for every SETUP, and (decisively) its outcome is observed for every SETUP in the data, taken or not. So the take/skip/size decision at the SETUP bar is a one-step problem with full-information feedback: it is supervised meta-labelling in Lopez de Prado's sense, not a bandit (no off-policy correction is needed because the counterfactual is in the table) and not sequential RL (no position overlap: 0 of 1,003 Foundation trades overlap on 5m, by construction the next SETUP needs the CHoCH that exits the previous trade). Everything proposed below descends from that framing: the labels and weights (AFML ch. 3-4), the validation harness (ch. 7, 11-14), importance with substitution effects removed (ch. 8; MLAM ch. 6), calibrated sizing (ch. 10), conformal sets for the skip decision (Vovk; Angelopoulos and Bates), and break/explosiveness statistics as regime features (ch. 17). Sample-size reality drives the design: on 5m IS there are 823 SETUPs and 181 winners; the engine-label net has std 10,271 INR (holds run to 70 sessions because the engine has no square-off), so a kept-vs-skipped expectancy difference below about 1,400 INR per trade (400 vs 400 split, 5% two-sided) is undetectable on that label. The intraday label (exit forced at the entry session's 15:25 bar, the lab's ST1/ST2 book) is therefore the primary label in every study; the top decile of winners carries 46% of gross wins (win mean +10,878, loss mean -3,429), so every gate is judged on |net|-weighted winner recall and kept-vs-skipped expectancy plus the session-matched random control, never on accuracy or net alone (a gate that trades less always saves costs). Data facts the studies rely on: the 5-minute table at scratchpad/fz_v3/5minute (features.parquet, 186 columns, 143 as-of; 97 numeric with 114 pairs |rho| > 0.9; causality verified by the truncated build), the 1-minute table not yet landed (scripts 01-03 only) but promised with the same column contract (a few thousand SETUPs). Box: 4 logical cores, 7.9 GB RAM with about 1.2 GB free beside the other session's 1.1 GB lab process; every study is a single process under 500 MB and 25 CPU-minutes per timeframe, at most two at a time, no pip installs (numpy 2.2.6, sklearn 1.7.2, pandas 2.3.3, scipy 1.14.1, xgboost 3.2.0, shap 0.49.1, numba 0.65, joblib; statsmodels/mapie/mlfinlab/lightgbm/torch absent, so ADF, CUSUM, FFD, conformal and PBO are hand-coded in numpy, all short). Order and dependencies: the harness (study 2) first because every other study and H1-H5 consume its splitter and trials ledger; then meta-labelling (1) which also hands H5 its labels, weights, OOF probabilities and splitter instead of a second gradient-boosting run; importance (3) and regime (6) can run in parallel with (1) since they only need the splitter; conformal (4) and sizing (5) consume (1)'s OOF file and are cheap. Deliberately left out with reasons: sequential bootstrap (

- Why this lens splits the problem the way it does. (1) The take/skip choice at a Foundation SETUP is a contextual bandit with FULL information: Foundation took every SETUP, so the reward of "take" (fnd_net, 1m: 5,326 rows, 5m: 1,012 rows) is logged for every context, and the reward of "skip" is exactly 0 by definition. There is no unobserved arm, hence no propensity model, no inverse-propensity weighting and no doubly-robust correction: the off-policy value of ANY gate pi is computed exactly as sum over SETUPs of pi(x)*net(x). The only statistical problem is generalisation from a few thousand contexts, so the right tools are cost-sensitive policy learning (value-maximising policy trees, cost-proportionate weighting) and honest selection, not bandit exploration. (2) Sequential RL is genuinely justified only where today's action changes which future rewards remain reachable: the in-trade exit (hold/exit/partial each bar; 1m IS has ~186k intraday bar-steps inside positions, ~800k once trajectories are extended to the 15:25 square-off) and, at session level, whether to keep trading today. On a price-taker's tape the dynamics are exogenous (an Exo-MDP): any exit policy can be replayed exactly and the hindsight-optimal exit is computable per trade, so OPE (DR/MAGIC) is not the bottleneck; generalisation and multiplicity are. Deep offline RL (CQL, IQL, Decision Transformer) and neural generators (TimeGAN, diffusion) are not runnable here (no torch) and would be badly over-parameterised for 4.5k trajectories anyway; the studies say so and use the closest feasible analogues (pessimistic tree-ensemble FQI, hindsight-imitation, GMM-Markov and session-bootstrap tapes). (3) Sizing is a downstream Kelly problem that only exists once a positive-conditional-edge region is found; the raw book (win rate 15%, mean -922 INR) has negative Kelly, and the study is written to return "0 lots" honestly. (4) Costs are 1,050-1,120 INR per trade and the median 1m trade moves 9 pts, so a gate that trades less always raises net by the saved costs: every study judges on kept-vs-skipped expectancy, the session-matched random control at the same per-session position count (fz_report.random_control), the permutation p, and (new here) the multiplicity-adjusted SPA/PBO from session-block resampling. (5) Leakage discipline is shared: features from the as-of columns only (prefixes fnd_, fwd_, fzpos_, st7_ POST columns, swings.broken_final, events.window_end/end, zones/visits final-state fields are excluded), contiguous session-block CV with purge (drop training trades whose exit falls in the test block) and a 2-session embargo, OOS (2026-01-01..2026-09-25) touched once per study at the end; the 5-minute engine trades are re-cut at 15:25 from bars because the build carries no square-off (358 of 1,012 held overnight). Priority order: the gate (1), the exit policy (2), then the robustness/multiplicity certificate that must pass before any key ships (3), the certified operating point (4)

## Studies
======
### decision-making-1-fullinfo-bandit-policy-tree-gate (priority 1)

**technique.** Offline contextual bandit with full-information rewards, solved as cost-sensitive policy learning: value-maximising depth-limited policy trees (Athey-Wager / Zhou-Athey-Wager) and cost-proportionate weighted gradient boosting, with the policy value computed exactly (direct method, no IPS) and distilled to a rule list

**what_it_answers.** Which Foundation SETUPs to take and which to skip, by regime / time / volume / level / card context, chosen to maximise INR value (not accuracy), and whether the learned gate beats the session-matched random gate and the frozen ST7/ST8 gates on kept-vs-skipped expectancy rather than by trading less.

**method.** Inputs: fz_v3/minute/setup_features.parquet (5,326 rows, 118 as-of columns) and fz_v3/5minute/features.parquet (1,012 rows, 143 as-of columns). Reward table per SETUP: r_take = fnd_net (primary variant recomputed from bars with a 15:25 square-off on the entry session, stop as hard floor; secondary = the engine's own exit as built), r_skip = 0. Every gate pi has exact value V(pi) = mean(pi(x) * r_take); baselines: Foundation (pi = take), ST7/ST8 (st7_traded / fzpos_kind), session-matched random at the same per-session count. Learners on IS only: (A) exact depth-1 and greedy depth-2/3 policy trees whose split criterion is the policy value (sum of r_take over the take-leaf), min leaf 100 SETUPs (1m) / 40 (5m), implemented in numpy over ~110 features x 30 quantile thresholds; (B) HistGradientBoostingClassifier on y = sign(net) with sample_weight = |net| winsorised at the 1st/99th percentile (Zadrozny-Langford-Abe cost-proportionate reduction; with two arms and full information this is the regret-optimal reduction), policy = take iff P_w(win) > 0.5, plus HistGradientBoostingRegressor on winsorised net with policy take iff E[net|x] > tau, tau swept post hoc from out-of-fold predictions; (C) distillation: fit a depth-<=3 DecisionTreeClassifier (min leaf 100) to (B)'s out-of-fold decisions and extract <= 8 conjunctive rules; report fidelity to (B) and the distilled policy's own CV value. Selection on IS CV only: maximise kept-minus-skipped mean net subject to kept share >= 20% and kept n >= 300 (1m) / 80 (5m); also report the value with the top 1% winners removed (heavy tail: 1m winners median 1.8k, p90 10k INR). Diagnostics: SHAP (TreeExplainer) on (B) for the drivers; winner recall and loser precision; per-hour and per-regime kept share. OOS once: kept n, kept net, skipped net, expectancy difference, winner recall / loser precision, random-control percentile at matched per-session k (2,000 seeded draws), permutation p, calibration of E[net|x] by decile.

**leakage_controls.** Features restricted to the README's as-of columns; the ledger's session-so-far fields (today_net_asof etc.) are allowed because they use exits <= k. Excluded by name: fnd_*, fwd_*, fzpos_*, st7_outcome_gate and all st7_ POST columns, swings.broken_final, events.window_end/end, zones.retired_* and visits.end_* unless bar-conditioned. CV = 8 contiguous session blocks (GroupKFold on session_i, blocks kept in time order), purge = drop training SETUPs whose trade exit date falls inside the test block, embargo = 2 sessions after each test block. tau, tree depth, min-leaf and the kept-share floor are fixed above; any change is a new pre-registration. OOS evaluated exactly once with the frozen rule list; the winsorisation and quantile thresholds are computed on the training folds only.

**compute.** HistGB on 4.5k x 110: ~2 s per fit; 8 folds x 2 learners x 3 seeds ~ 2 min; exact depth-1 policy search 110 x 30 thresholds trivial, greedy depth-3 ~ 1 min; SHAP seconds; controls (2,000 draws x 1,026 sessions) ~ 1 min. Total < 10 CPU-min per timeframe, peak memory < 400 MB.

**libraries.** numpy, pandas, pyarrow, scikit-learn 1.7.2 (HistGradientBoosting, DecisionTree, GroupKFold), shap 0.49.1, numba (optional for the threshold sweep)

**output_as_config.** strategy_13.json / strategy_14.json block "gate": {"kind": "rule_list", "default": "take"|"skip", "rules": [{"if": {"reg_n_choch_since_bos": [">=", 2], "hour_bin": ["in", ["11","12"]]}, "then": "skip"}, ...] (<= 8 rules, <= 3 conditions each), "min_expected_net_inr": tau, "provenance": {"source": "learned on IS 2021-10..2025-12", "script": "<name>", "sha": "<sha>", "cv_kept_minus_skipped_inr": ..., "control_pct": ...}}. Every feature named in a rule must be one the lab can compute at the SETUP bar from the card, the engine events and the bars; the GBM never ships.

**novelty.** Athey & Wager 2021 (Policy learning with observational data) and Zhou, Athey & Wager 2023 (Offline multi-action policy learning: exact depth-limited policy trees) supply the value-maximising tree; Zadrozny, Langford & Abe 2003 (cost-proportionate example weighting) and Beygelzimer & Langford 2009 (offset tree) are the bandit-to-classification reductions, which become exact here because the reward of both arms is known (Dudik, Langford & Li 2011's doubly-robust estimator collapses to the direct method). Distillation follows Bastani, Kim & Bastani 2018 (policy extraction into decision trees). This differs from H5 in the objective: H5 fits win/loss; this maximises INR value with the skip reward pinned at 0 and the costs inside the reward.

**Judge 1** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 3 · keep True — fix: Trap: a value-maximising split on heavy-tailed rewards chases the leaf holding the outlier winners (1m p90 winner 10k INR vs median 1.8k), tau 'swept post hoc' on pooled OOF is a selection the ledger must count, and this is study 2's hypothesis run a second time under a different splitter (8 vs 12 blocks), doubling the trials for one question. Fix: keep the 1/99 winsorisation and make the top-1%-removed value a hard pass condition, add a block-wise sign test (kept-vs-skipped > 0 in >= 6 of 8 blocks), log every tau, use the harness splitter, restrict features to study 3's shortlist, and merge with study 2 into one trial family so exactly one gate candidate from the family reaches OOS.

**Judge 2** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 4 · keep True — fix: Merge with quant-ml-canon-meta-label-gate (same reward, same |net|-weighted HGB); keep the exact depth-limited policy tree as the distinct, most config-native learner. Nest tau: 'tau swept post hoc from out-of-fold predictions' selects on all IS OOF outcomes; choose tau inside each training fold as the meta-label study does. Adopt the harness splitter (12 blocks, 3-session embargo; 3 is justified by the 5m room age and vol_med60 memory, 2 is not) instead of 8 blocks / 2 sessions. Keep the kept-share and kept-n floors and the top-1%-removed value; they belong in the harness go/no-go for everyone. < 10 CPU-min, < 400 MB: runs now.
======
**compute.** < 2 CPU-min, < 200 MB (numpy/scipy on <= 5k rows x 2,000 draws).

**libraries.** numpy, pandas, scipy.optimize, scikit-learn 1.7.2 (HistGradientBoostingRegressor quantile loss, IsotonicRegression)

**output_as_config.** strategy_13/14.json "position": {"lots": 3, "size_by_edge": [{"edge_min_inr": 0, "lots": 1}, {"edge_min_inr": 800, "lots": 2}, {"edge_min_inr": 2000, "lots": 3}], "kelly": {"fraction": 0.5, "capital_inr": 420000, "drawdown_cap": 0.2}} with provenance; "edge" is the same rule-list score study 1 ships, so no new feature is needed in the lab. If no bucket has f_s > 0 the block is omitted and the finding is recorded in S49.

**novelty.** Kelly 1956 and Thorp 2006 (growth-optimal sizing); MacLean, Thorp & Ziemba 2010 (fractional Kelly and its risk-growth trade-off); Busseti, Ryu & Boyd 2016 (risk-constrained Kelly gambling with a drawdown constraint as a convex problem); Baker & McHale 2013 (Kelly under parameter uncertainty, shrinkage). Sizing is treated as a policy downstream of a calibrated bandit value, not as a standalone optimisation, which is what keeps it from amplifying an overfit gate.

**Judge 1** feasible 5 · rigour 3 · expected value 1 · keep False — fix: Trap: quantile regression of net on ~180 winners; Kelly on a book whose raw edge is negative returns 0 lots by construction, which the study already states; duplicate of study 5. Fix: do not run until a gate has passed OOS; then the one-table version of study 5 with charges per lot held at the 1-lot rate.

**Judge 2** feasible 5 · rigour 4 · expected value 2 · keep False — fix: Duplicate of quant-ml-canon-bet-sizing on a book whose gated edge is not yet shown positive (raw Kelly is negative at 15-22% win rate). Merge the two into one conditional sizing step that runs only after a gate passes the harness go/no-go; ship the monotone <= 3-step lots schedule only if a bucket has CPCV 5th-percentile net-per-lot improvement > 0, else record 'lots = 1 or skip'. Per-signal lots is a lab change: ask the user before any key is written.

### decision-making-6-session-stop-rule-finite-horizon (priority 6)

**technique.** Session-level stopping rule as a finite-horizon MDP with exact replay: stop trading for the day after k stop-outs or a loss L, tested against the null that the session ledger so far carries no information about the next SETUP

**what_it_answers.** Whether the causal session ledger (today_net_asof, today_n_stops_asof, today_n_setups_before; 1m median 8 SETUPs per active session, max 20) predicts the next SETUP's net at all, and whether a daily stop rule adds expectancy beyond the cost it saves by trading less (the pure cost-avoidance trap in its simplest form).

"""Reinforcement learning over the Foundation SETUPs (entry_rule rl_v1): a journal of every trade and a learner that decides,
at each SETUP, whether to trade and how - the exit profile, the stop distance and the number of lots - and updates itself
after every closed trade.

What the learner is
  A contextual bandit with Bayesian linear regression per action (linear Thompson sampling). One decision per SETUP,
  from features known at the SETUP candle's close (time of day, ATR, distance from the two AVWAPs, trend flip, bars since
  the CHoCH, the day's CHoCH count, the session's results so far, recent form). Actions: skip, or (exit profile x stop x
  lots) from the strategy file's `rl` block; an intraday profile is not an option at or after its square-off time. It learns
  with full information: once a SETUP's candles have played out, the outcome of EVERY feasible action for that SETUP is
  known from the price data, so every action's model is updated - not only the one taken. Updates are applied strictly in
  time order: an outcome is used only once its exit candle has closed, so no decision sees the future (tests/test_rl.py
  checks this by truncation, at random candles and right after SETUP candles).
  Under full information the exploration term plays no learning role (every action's model updates on every SETUP); it
  only randomises near-ties and shrinks as 1/sqrt(updates), so after a few hundred SETUPs a decision is close to the argmax
  of 27 posterior means. That maximum is biased upward (the winner's curse): `pred` runs above the realised reward of the
  trades taken; the payload reports the gap and the correlation between pred and realised reward so it can be read.
  Lots are chosen by expected reward alone: there is no risk or drawdown term.

Rewards (the strategy file picks one; the three are run as separate strategies). Each is a per-lot value, clipped to +-10
per lot so one outlier cannot swamp a linear model, times the lots, so sizing stays learnable:
  net  net rupees after slippage and charges, per lot, in units of one lot's 50-point risk (lot_size x 50)
  r    the position's R multiple: net points per lot divided by the stop distance
  pf   as net, with losses weighted x1.5 (profit-factor oriented: fewer, cleaner trades)
  skip always earns 0.
  A loss is bounded by the stop (about 5 units at most), a trailing win is not, so the clip cuts the right tail only - most
  often on the multi-lot trailing arms; the payload counts the clipped outcomes per action.
  The reward of an action is its own outcome at that SETUP. The learner's BOOK holds one position per contract (the lab's
  strike lock), so a long-held action also costs the book the SETUPs it locks out - and that cost is in no reward. The
  learner is therefore biased toward the positional profiles relative to their value to the book; read the action mix
  beside the locked count (STRATEGY_ANALYSIS_TODO S51).

Learning window
  The learner starts empty at the FIRST session of the futures file (Oct 2021) and learns through every SETUP to the file's
  end, once per strategy; each backtest is a window cut from that one run (its decisions up to any date do not depend on
  later data). Inside a window the trades are scored, charted and journaled as `scored`; the SETUPs before it are the
  learning history. So a 2026 window is out-of-sample for the knowledge the learner starts it with, and the learner keeps
  learning during it, as it would live. Every book is valued at the window's last candle for lots still open there, and a
  month straddling the window's start is reported as two rows (learning, scored).

Yardsticks, reported beside the learner (every book holds one position per contract, like the learner):
  BASE book      the strategy file's first profile at stop 50 with the most lots - Strategy 9's rule - at every feasible
                 SETUP its own open position does not lock
  RANDOM books   `control_draws` (default 200) seeded books, each a uniformly random action per SETUP (skip is 1 of 28, so
                 they take almost every free SETUP, 2 lots on average); the learner's percentile among them is reported and
                 draw 0 is the journal's Random column. Beating them is necessary, not sufficient.
  PERMUTATIONS   `control_draws` matched controls: the learner's own decisions in the window, shuffled across the window's
                 SETUPs in time order (the same action multiset, so the same take rate and sizes; an action a SETUP cannot
                 take goes to the next free one). The learner's percentile among them, and the share at or above it, test
                 WHERE it chose to trade.
  SEED SPREAD    the learner run again from empty with `spread_seeds` (default 4 more seeds): the window net of each. Four
                 features and the lock depend on the learner's own path, so one seed is one path; the spread is the first
                 thing to read. The backtest windows are cuts of one run and nested, not independent checks.
  ORACLE         the best NET among the feasible actions per SETUP in hindsight, skip included, so never below 0 at a
                 SETUP; the maximum of 27 noisy outcomes summed - an upper bound, not a target to capture a share of.

v1 scope: near-month futures only (the Futures type); option types and a backtest's square-off override are refused with a
reason (each exit profile carries its own square-off). Costs, the strike lock and the fill rules are the lab's (lab.manage /
lab.price_trade); a contract whose candles end before its expiry date closes the lots at its last candle ('expiry').
Deterministic: fixed seeds in the strategy file.

def load_tape(folder, label="L1"):
    """harness.load for a tape folder: the L1 units (traded, l1_taken) as a harness.Table."""
    F = pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(folder, "features.parquet"))
    TR = pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(folder, "trades.parquet")).set_index("entry_i")
    S = pd.read_parquet(os.path.join(folder, "sessions.parquet"))
    tf = json.load(open(os.path.join(folder, "meta.json")))["timeframe"]
    F = F[F.traded.astype(bool)]
    if label == "L1": F = F[F.l1_taken.astype(bool)]
    F = F.sort_values("setup_i").reset_index(drop=True)
    TR = TR.loc[F.setup_i.to_numpy()].reset_index()
    return H.Table(tf, label, F, TR, S)


def evaluate_keep(T, keep, tag, controls=True, draws=H.CONTROL_DRAWS):
    """Kept-vs-skipped metrics of a keep mask over the tape's IS rows (every tape row is IS), through harness.metrics."""
    rows = np.flatnonzero(T.is_mask)
    m = H.metrics(T, np.asarray(keep, dtype=bool), rows, tag, controls=controls, draws=draws)
    return m



def read_health(folder, compute=True):
    p = os.path.join(folder, "tape_health.json")
    if os.path.exists(p): return json.load(open(p, encoding="utf-8"))
    return tape_health(folder) if compute else None


def all_tape_folders(tf, gen=None):
    """Every built tape folder of the timeframe (and generator), sorted by generator then seed index k (numeric)."""
    pat = os.path.join(HERE, "tapes", tf, f"{gen or '*'}_*")
    fs = [p for p in glob.glob(pat) if os.path.exists(os.path.join(p, "features.parquet"))]
    return sorted(fs, key=lambda p: (_tape_gen(p), _tape_k(p)))


def tape_folders(tf, gen=None, healthy=True, n=None, original_only=False):
    """The tape set a candidate is evaluated on.
    healthy=True (default, the CERTIFICATE set): per generator the first n (= DESIGN_N[tf]) tapes by seed index k whose
    tape_health.json says healthy (computed when missing). healthy=False: every tape built (n=None) or the first n per generator.
    original_only=True restricts to k < DESIGN_N[tf] (the tapes of the first build, locked ones included when healthy=False)."""
    n = DESIGN_N[tf] if n is None and healthy else n
    out = []
    for g in sorted({_tape_gen(p) for p in all_tape_folders(tf, gen)}):
        fs = all_tape_folders(tf, g)
        if original_only: fs = [p for p in fs if _tape_k(p) < DESIGN_N[tf]]
        if healthy: fs = [p for p in fs if read_health(p)["healthy"]]
        if n is not None: fs = fs[:n]
        out.extend(fs)
    return out


# ---------------------------------------------------------------- the pass rule (FINDINGS section 7) as go_no_go-shaped items
def null_tape_check_from_diffs(real_diff, diffs, session_same_sign_min=PASS_RULE["session_same_sign_min"]):
    """diffs = {'gmm': [...], 'segment': [...], 'session': [...]} (one diff per certificate tape). Returns (passed, checks, summary):
    checks are (ok, value) pairs like harness.go_no_go's; passed = real diff > gmm p95 AND > segment p95 AND the session tapes
    carry the real sign in >= 75% of tapes."""
    q = lambda v, p: (round(float(np.nanquantile(v, p)), 2) if len(v) and np.isfinite(v).any() else None)
    ch, summ = {}, {}
    for g in ("gmm", "segment"):
        v = np.asarray(diffs.get(g, []), dtype=float); p95 = q(v, 0.95)
        ch[f"null_tape:real_diff>{g}_p95"] = (real_diff is not None and p95 is not None and real_diff > p95, p95)
        summ[g] = dict(n=int(len(v)), p50=q(v, 0.5), p95=q(v, 0.95), real_pct=(round(float(100 * np.nanmean(v < real_diff)), 1) if len(v) and real_diff is not None else None))
    v = np.asarray(diffs.get("session", []), dtype=float)
    same = float(np.nanmean(np.sign(v) == np.sign(real_diff))) if len(v) and real_diff is not None else None
    ch[f"null_tape:session_same_sign>={session_same_sign_min}"] = (same is not None and same >= session_same_sign_min, round(same, 3) if same is not None else None)
    summ["session"] = dict(n=int(len(v)), p50=q(v, 0.5), p95=q(v, 0.95), same_sign_share=(round(same, 3) if same is not None else None))
    summ["null_tape_diff_inr"] = {g: {"p50": summ[g]["p50"], "p95": summ[g]["p95"]} for g in ("gmm", "segment", "session") if g in summ}
    return all(v[0] for v in ch.values()), ch, summ


def null_tape_check(real_diff, tf, rules, controls=False, draws=H.CONTROL_DRAWS, label="L1", verbose=False):
    """The FINDINGS section 7 pass rule for a candidate rule list: evaluate it on the certificate tapes (tape_folders(tf, gen),
    healthy, the design count per generator), compare the real-tape diff (the candidate's ledger row) with the gmm / segment p95
    and the session sign share. Returns (passed, checks, summary); summary['per_tape'] holds every tape's result. Tape numbers
    never enter the ledger. Call it only after the candidate's real-tape ledger row exists (the tapes are not a search space)."""
    per, diffs = [], {}
    for g in ("gmm", "segment", "session"):
        diffs[g] = []
        for folder in tape_folders(tf, g):
            r = evaluate_rule_list(folder, rules, controls=controls, draws=draws, label=label)
            r.update(gen=g, k=_tape_k(folder)); per.append(r); diffs[g].append(np.nan if r["diff"] is None else r["diff"])
            if verbose: print(f"  {g}_{r['k']}: diff {r['diff']} kept_share {r['kept_share']}", flush=True)
    passed, ch, summ = null_tape_check_from_diffs(real_diff, diffs)
    summ.update(tf=tf, real_diff=real_diff, per_tape=per, tape_set="certificate (healthy, first DESIGN_N per generator)")

20	## 1. Definitions (fixed before the numbers)
21	
22	- **Entries**: the L1 units, entry at the SETUP bar's close in the SETUP's direction; 1 min = Strategy 1 rules (prev_swing stop), 5 min = Strategy 2 rules (choch_candle stop).
23	- **Square-off bar**: the last bar of the entry session opening at or before 15:25 (`lab.eod_cut`); **cap** = min(square-off bar, the contract's last candle) — every comparator is cut there.
24	- **Foundation stop**: `features.sl`, engine touch convention (open beyond the stop -> fill at the open; wick touch -> fill at the stop; a session's first bar -> the close). Identical to `lab.manage`'s stop (proved on every IS trade, section 2).
25	- **Extended trajectory** (learners A / B, the floor oracle): bars entry+1 .. J_end, J_end = the Foundation stop bar when it fires before the cap, else the cap. Exits before J_end are at the bar's close; at J_end the exit is the stop fill or the cap close. The engine's next-CHoCH exit is not applied (Exo-MDP: the tape does not react, so every exit policy is replayable).
26	- **Value**: net INR per trade per lot = `lab.price_trade` arithmetic (lot 65, 5 pts slippage per side, `lab.trade_charges(ZERODHA_NFO_FUT)` on the slipped prices); a 3-lot ladder is reported per position and per lot (position net / 3); selection and every comparison use per lot.
27	- **Oracle (free)**: the best close exit over entry+1 .. cap with no stop (an upper bound for any close-exit policy; a target filled intrabar can exceed it by at most that bar's range). **Oracle (floor)**: the best exit on the extended trajectory, ties -> earliest (learner B's target). **Exit regret** = oracle - policy.
28	- **Random-exit control**: exit at a uniformly drawn bar of entry+1 .. cap at its close, 2,000 seeded draws (`fz|exit`); a policy's percentile = share of draws whose mean net per lot is below the policy's (+ half the ties).
29	- **CHoCH against**: an `events.parquet` CHoCH with i > entry, i <= t, direction opposite to the position (known at its own bar under touch rules). **Time stop N**: exit at the close of bar entry+N if still open.
30	- **Cut convention (learner C)**: the time stop and the CHoCH-against exit are a post-processing cut of `lab.manage`'s tranches: every tranche whose lab exit bar is later than the cut bar exits at the cut bar's close instead; a tranche the lab closed at or before the cut bar keeps its exit (the stop / target on the cut bar is assumed first, as `lab.manage` assumes the stop first on a candle); with both cuts on, the earlier bar wins.
31	- **Learner C grid** (never shrunk): stop {35, 50, 75 pts, Foundation stop via `exact_R`} x scale_out {none, 1R, 2R, 3R, 4R with 1 lot (the target is the exit), ladder 1R/2R, ladder 2R/4R with 3 lots} x trail {none, (2,1), (2,2), (3,1), (3,2), (4,1), (4,2)} x time stop {none, 30, 60, 120 bars} x CHoCH-against {off, on}; square_off 15:25 always: 196 `lab.manage` positions x 8 cuts = **1,568 variants per timeframe**, each a strategy-row dict as `rl.py` builds it (lot 65, slippage 5, `position_json`, cap = the contract's last candle as `rl.contract_end`).
32	- **Selection (C)**: nested in `harness.purged_splits` (argmax of the training fold's mean net per lot, applied to the test fold) and in the 66 CPCV splits -> 11 paths (`harness.cpcv_paths`). **Learners A / B**: 3 contiguous session-block folds (harness blocks 0-3 / 4-7 / 8-11), purge of training trades whose trajectory intersects the test fold's bars, 3-session embargo; B's p* by an inner 3-fold on the training fold; A's Q-ensembles refit per fold.
33	- **Multiplicity**: every variant and every learner is a row of the append-only `exit_ledger.jsonl` + `vectors/*.npz` (harness-compatible per-session vectors: kept = the variant, skipped / all = the Foundation L1 exit on the same entries, so `harness.pbo(vecs, 'diff')`, `harness.spa`, `harness.effective_trials`, `harness.bootstrap_ci` read them unchanged). The harness ledger (`OUT/ledger/`) is for gates; this study writes to it only the gate x exit rows of section 8.
34	- **Pass rule** for an exit candidate (adapted from `harness.GO` to a policy-vs-Foundation difference on frozen entries): nested-CV diff > 0; CPCV 5th percentile diff > 0; random-exit percentile >= 95; 12-block sign-flip one-sided p <= 0.05 with >= 8 blocks positive; **lower bound of the 90% block-bootstrap CI of the diff > 0** (`boot_ci90_lower>0`, as `harness.go_no_go` implements it: a CI entirely below 0 fails; the earlier wording 'CI excludes 0' was loose — repair, section 11); **diff with the top 1% winners removed > 0** (the harness's pre-registered `diff_top1_removed` item: the trades whose policy net is in its own top 1% are dropped, the paired diff is averaged over the rest — `diff_top1_winners_removed` in `eval_table_*.csv`); PBO <= 0.2; studentised SPA p <= 0.10 over the family (the family's vectors at the label's 2-dp precision — repair, section 11). **Disclosure (repair)**: the earlier text of this rule read 'diff with the top 1% of per-trade *gains* removed > 0' (`diff_top1_gains_removed`: the trades whose gain over the Foundation exit is in the top 1% are dropped). That variant was written after learner C's results had been read (this script's own docstring) and is negative-biased by construction: removing the top 1% of a dispersed difference lowers its mean even when the true mean is zero (its zero-mean reference, the same trim on the centred difference, is about -150 INR on 1 min). It is reported beside the pass item with that reference and is not used to decide.

entries.name: Monitor
entries.description:
Start a background monitor that streams events from a long-running script. Each stdout line is an event — you keep working and notifications arrive in the chat. Events arrive on their own schedule and are not replies from the user, even if one lands while you're waiting for the user to answer a question.

Pick by how many notifications you need:
- **One** ("tell me when the server is ready / the build finishes") → use **Bash with `run_in_background`** and a command that exits when the condition is true, e.g. `until grep -q "Ready in" dev.log; do sleep 0.5; done`. You get a single completion notification when it exits.
- **One per occurrence, until the monitor expires (re-arm to continue)** ("tell me every time an ERROR line appears") → Monitor with an unbounded command (`tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, `while true`).
- **One per occurrence, until a known end** ("emit each CI step result, stop when the run completes") → Monitor with a command that emits lines and then exits.

Your script's stdout is the event stream. Each line becomes a notification. Exit ends the watch.

  # Each matching log line is an event
  tail -f /var/log/app.log | grep --line-buffered "ERROR"

  # Each file change is an event
  inotifywait -m --format '%e %f' /watched/dir

  # Poll GitHub for new PR comments and emit one line per new comment
  last=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
  while true; do
    now=$(date -u +%Y-%m-%dT%H:%M:%SZ)
    gh api "repos/owner/repo/issues/123/comments?since=$last" --jq '.[] | "\(.user.login): \(.body)"'
    last=$now; sleep 30
  done

  # Node script that emits events as they arrive (e.g. WebSocket listener)
  node watch-for-events.js

  # Per-occurrence with a natural end: emit each CI check as it lands, exit when the run completes
  prev=""
  while true; do
    s=$(gh pr checks 123 --json name,bucket)
    cur=$(jq -r '.[] | select(.bucket!="pending") | "\(.name): \(.bucket)"' <<<"$s" | sort)
    comm -13 <(echo "$prev") <(echo "$cur")
    prev=$cur
    jq -e 'all(.bucket!="pending")' <<<"$s" >/dev/null && break
    sleep 30
  done

**Don't use an unbounded command for a single notification.** `tail -f`, `inotifywait -m`, and `while true` never exit on their own, so the monitor stays armed until timeout even after the event has fired. For "tell me when X is ready," use Bash `run_in_background` with an `until` loop instead (one notification, ends in seconds). Note that `tail -f log | grep -m 1 ...` does *not* fix this: if the log goes quiet after the match, `tail` never receives SIGPIPE and the pipeline hangs anyway.

**Script quality:**
- Every pipe stage must flush per line or matches sit in its buffer unseen: `grep` needs `--line-buffered`, `awk` needs `fflush()`. `head` cannot flush at all — `| head -N` delivers nothing until N matches accumulate, then ends the stream.
- In poll loops, handle transient failures (`curl ... || true`) — one failed request shouldn't kill the monitor.
- Poll intervals: 30s+ for remote APIs (rate limits), 0.5-1s for local checks.
- Write a specific `description` — it appears in every notification ("errors in deploy.log" not "watching logs").
- Only stdout is the event stream. Stderr goes to the output file (readable via Read) but does not trigger notifications — for a command you run directly (e.g. `python train.py 2>&1 | grep --line-buffered ...`), merge stderr with `2>&1` so its failures reach your filter. (No effect on `tail -f` of an existing log — that file only contains what its writer redirected.)

**Coverage — silence is not success.** When watching a job or process for an outcome, your filter must match every terminal state, not just the happy path. A monitor that greps only for the success marker stays silent through a crashloop, a hung process, or an unexpected exit — and silence looks identical to "still running." Before arming, ask: *if this process crashed right now, would my filter emit anything?* If not, widen it.

  # Wrong — silent on crash, hang, or any non-success exit
  tail -f run.log | grep --line-buffered "elapsed_steps="

  # Right — one alternation covering progress + the failure signatures you'd act on
  tail -f run.log | grep -E --line-buffered "elapsed_steps=|Traceback|Error|FAILED|assert|Killed|OOM"

For poll loops checking job state, emit on every terminal status (`succeeded|failed|cancelled|timeout`), not just success. If you cannot confidently enumerate the failure signatures, broaden the grep alternation rather than narrow it — some extra noise is better than missing a crashloop.

**Output volume**: Every stdout line is a conversation message, so the filter should be selective — but selective means "the lines you'd act on," not "only good news." Never pipe raw logs; filter to exactly the success and failure signals you care about. Monitors that produce too many events are automatically stopped; restart with a tighter filter if this happens.

Stdout lines within 200ms are batched into a single notification, so multiline output from a single event groups naturally.

The script runs in the same shell environment as Bash. Exit ends the watch (exit code is reported). Every monitor expires after `timeout_ms` (default 5 minutes, at most 30 minutes): it is killed and you get one notice with the event count. Re-arm it if you still need the watch; for a long watch (PR monitoring, log tails) set `timeout_ms` to the maximum and re-arm on each expiry, and widen the filter if an expiry with no events was unexpected. Use TaskStop to cancel early.
**ws source** — open a WebSocket and stream each incoming text frame as an event. No shell, no polling: the server pushes, you get notified.

  Monitor({
    ws: {url: 'wss://events.example.com/stream', protocols: ['v1']},
    description: 'deploy events',
  })

Each text frame becomes one notification (multiline frames stay as one event). Binary frames are reported as `[binary frame, N bytes]` rather than passed through. Socket close ends the watch with the close code surfaced; errors are surfaced before close. Same rate limiting as bash — a firehose will be suppressed and eventually stopped, so subscribe to a filtered feed where one exists.

Prefer this over `command: 'websocat wss://…'` — it avoids the extra process and line-buffering pitfalls. Use bash when you need to transform or filter frames with shell tools before they become events.

description.description: Short human-readable description of what you are monitoring (shown in notifications).

timeout_ms.description: Kill the monitor after this deadline. Default 300000ms. Deadlines above 1800000ms are capped to 1800000ms. You are notified at expiry and can re-arm.

command.description: Shell command or script. Each stdout line is an event; exit ends the watch.

ws.description: WebSocket to open. Each text frame is an event; binary frames are reported as a placeholder line. Socket close ends the watch. Cannot be combined with command.
